function.name: equals a value
function.description: Keeps the rows where a String field is exactly this value.
function.semantics: Written with the constant first so a null field value returns false instead of throwing a NullPointerException.

function.name: equals a value, ignoring case
function.description: Keeps the rows where a String field has this value in any case.
function.semantics: The constant comes first, a null field value returns false.

function.name: contains a piece of text
function.description: Keeps the rows where a String field contains a piece of text, a space in this example.
function.semantics: The null check comes first, the field is only touched when it has a value.

function.name: starts with / ends with
function.description: Keeps the rows where a String field starts and ends with a piece of text.
function.semantics: Every String method of Java is available on a String field.

function.name: matches a regular expression
function.description: Keeps the rows where a String field matches a regular expression.
function.semantics: matches() has to match the whole value, use find() semantics by surrounding the pattern with .*

function.name: is empty or blank
function.description: Keeps the rows where a String field has no usable value.
function.semantics: Hop reads an empty String as null in a lot of places, so both are checked.

function.name: is one of a list of values
function.description: Keeps the rows where a String field is one of a fixed list of values.
function.semantics: Use the fully qualified class name, the expression has no import statements.

function.name: compare an Integer field
function.description: Keeps the rows where an Integer field is larger than a value.
function.semantics: An Integer field arrives as a java.lang.Long. Check for null first, comparing a null value throws a NullPointerException when it is unboxed.

function.name: between two values
function.description: Keeps the rows where a field is inside a range.
function.semantics: && and || work like they do in Java, the first false stops the evaluation.

function.name: compare a Number field
function.description: Keeps the rows where a Number field is larger than a value.
function.semantics: A Number field arrives as a java.lang.Double.

function.name: even or odd
function.description: Keeps the rows with an even value, e.g. to split a stream in two.
function.semantics: All Java operators are available.

function.name: after a fixed date
function.description: Keeps the rows where a Date field is after a given date.
function.semantics: A Date field arrives as a java.util.Date. Months start at 0 in GregorianCalendar.

function.name: in the past
function.description: Keeps the rows where a Date field lies before the moment the row is evaluated.
function.semantics: new java.util.Date() is evaluated for every row.

function.name: a Boolean field is true
function.description: Keeps the rows where a Boolean field is true.
function.semantics: Writing it this way is null safe, active == Boolean.TRUE compares references and a null value throws when it is unboxed.

function.name: a field has no value
function.description: Keeps the rows where a field is null.
function.semantics: Fields arrive as objects, a null value is a null object.

function.name: a field has a value, with a default
function.description: Treats an empty or null field as a default value.
function.semantics: HopFunctions.nvl() is available in the condition, like it is in the User Defined Java Expression transform.

function.category: Examples - Fields not in every stream
function.name: the stream has this field
function.description: Keeps the rows of streams that have a field with this name.
function.semantics: row is always available and reads the row by field name. A field that is only used through row.* is never referenced by the expression itself, so the condition also compiles for streams that do not have it.

function.category: Examples - Fields not in every stream
function.name: filter on a field that is not in every stream
function.description: Filters on a field when the stream has it, and keeps every row when it does not.
function.semantics: This is the pattern for pipelines that read a layout which is only known at runtime, e.g. a Table Input transform reading select * from a table name in a variable.

function.category: Examples - Fields not in every stream
function.name: read a field by name
function.description: Reads a field by name instead of by referring to it directly.
function.semantics: row.getString(), getInteger(), getNumber(), getBigNumber(), getDate() and getBoolean() all return null when the stream has no field with that name.

function.name: compare with a variable
function.description: Compares a field with the value of a variable or parameter.
function.semantics: Variables are resolved before the expression is compiled, so they are used as text. Keep the quotes around the variable, the expression sees its value.

function.name: the whole condition in a variable
function.description: Builds the condition itself at runtime.
function.semantics: Because variables are resolved before the expression is compiled, a variable can hold the complete condition. A previous pipeline can set it to true for streams that need no filtering at all.
